title: Measure a wooden bar and enter its length
instruction: Use the tape measure on the right to measure the longest edge of the wooden bar behind it. Seat the hook at one end with the zero aligned, then pull the blade beyond the other end, within 10 degrees of the bar's long axis. Enter the measured length as an integer in millimetres on the calculator on the left, then press = to submit and finish. The tape measure retracts automatically when released; it has no lock. Complete the task within 120 seconds.
context: Workshop and assembly work often requires measuring an unlabelled part and entering its dimension into a tool. This task combines handling a spring-return measuring tape, reading its scale and physically entering the result.
setup: Standard YAM workbench: a purple plastic 21-key calculator (140 x 102 x 18 mm) at front left; an upright black/yellow plastic/rubber tape case (76 x 42 x 68 mm) at front right, steel hook facing left; and an unlabelled solid pine bar behind both. Bar length is uniformly sampled from integer 150-200 mm using the configured seed; width/height are 70 mm. Props are free to move. Initial poses are fixed and listed in README; seed 0 gives 193 mm.
scoring: Highest stage before the first = or 120 s: 0.25 for hook/bar contact with zero within 1 mm of either end plane; 0.5 if simultaneously the exposed blade extends beyond the opposite end and is within 10 degrees of the long axis; 1 if this measurement is followed by the correct integer submission within 120 s. Otherwise retain the achieved stage, or 0 if none. Stages persist after retraction; no hold time is required. A correct answer without measurement earns 0.
run_limit: 2,400 control steps at 20 Hz: 120 simulation seconds. Network waiting does not advance physics.
reset_notes: Use the configured seed to select the bar length and restore the documented object and robot poses. Clear the calculator, retract the tape, and settle the free props for 2 seconds before starting the clock.
fidelity: Rigid case and steel hook with a passive straight prismatic spring return; no lock, blade bending or internal coil. The graduated blade is visual and has no intermediate contact. Calculator keys use physical spring-loaded sliders. Masses, friction and springs are approximate. All execution uses CPU PhysX TGS at 240 Hz, native YAM actuators and the same 14-D position/gripper interface at 20 Hz.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.0/1.0 in 120 s; open-loop demo: 1.0/1.0 in 113.5 s.
